headline: Benchmarking RNA-seq methods for copy number, fusion calling and cell annotation
label: Sequencing Method Benchmarking
summary: Expanding single-cell, spatial and long-read RNA-seq use makes method choice and simulation-based benchmarking central to trustworthy biological inference.
synthesis: The common thread is benchmarking and validation of computational inference from RNA-seq data, spanning copy number, fusion detection, cell annotation, pathway scoring and differential expression. Several items pair methods with ground truth: stCNASim provides an allele-aware spatial simulator for benchmarking five copy number inference methods across 46 synthetic datasets, scROMA includes a ground-truth simulation framework, and scATrans is benchmarked against metabolic labeling. A six-caller long-read study reports false positives as the dominant error mode in fusion detection, and a multi-lab study spanning 42 labs and 207 pipelines uses Quartet and MAQC references to establish practices for alternative splicing analysis. What is new is reference-free inference, as in REFCON for copy number and Binary-SPA for spatial cell annotation, which removes dependence on normal-cell or reference annotations. This thread does not extend uniformly to every item; scXpand and CELLIA are primarily method frameworks without a comparable benchmarking emphasis.
